questions.question: What does it mean for $f$ to be right-continuous at $x_0$?
options: For $x$ sufficiently close to $x_0$ with $x \lt x_0$, the values $f(x)$ are close to $0$.
The value $f(x_0)$ must be the largest value of $f$ near $x_0$.
The function must be defined on all of $\mathbb{R}$.
For $x$ sufficiently close to $x_0$ with $x\ \ge x_0$, the values $f(x)$ are close to $f(x_0)$.

Only points $x$ with $x_0\ \le x \lt x_0+\delta$.
Only points $x$ with $x = x_0+\delta$.
